articles.title: India Cracks The Kalashnikov Code: First 100% Indigenous AK-203 ‘Sher’ Roars In Amethi
articles.description: India has crossed a major small-arms manufacturing milestone. Indo-Russian Rifles Private Limited has produced and successfully fired the first AK-203 ‘Sher’ made with 100% Indian components and input materials at Korwa in Amethi. The programme began as an Indo-Russian joint venture in 2019, but localisation has steadily transformed licensed production into an Indian supply chain. Each AK-203 involves roughly 50 components, 180 sub-parts and 120 manufacturing processes. IRRPL is contracted to supply 601,427 rifles under a roughly ₹5,200-crore programme and plans to finish deliveries by December 2030—22 months ahead of schedule. Production is designed to reach one rifle roughly every 100 seconds. The next test is Army evaluation of the fully indigenous configuration.
